dataset: TPC-DS SF100TCL — Retail Decision Support Benchmark
scale_description: 100 TB scale factor dataset. 100M customers, 500K+ items, ~300B rows in STORE_SALES, ~560B total fact rows. Always include date filters to control query cost.

metrics.name: Total Revenue
metrics.definition: Sum of extended sales price across all line items. This is gross revenue before coupons.
metrics.calculation: SUM(SS_EXT_SALES_PRICE) for store, SUM(CS_EXT_SALES_PRICE) for catalog, SUM(WS_EXT_SALES_PRICE) for web

metrics.name: Net Paid
metrics.definition: Revenue after coupon discounts are applied but before tax. The actual cash collected excluding tax.

metrics.name: Net Profit
metrics.definition: Net paid minus wholesale cost. Represents the retailer's margin on a sale. Can be negative if items are sold below cost.

metrics.name: Gross Margin %
metrics.definition: Percentage of revenue that is profit after cost of goods. Excludes operating expenses.

metrics.name: Return Rate
metrics.definition: Percentage of units sold that were subsequently returned. Use quantity-based, not revenue-based, as the primary metric.
metrics.calculation: SUM(return_quantity) / NULLIF(SUM(sold_quantity), 0) * 100 — requires joining SALES to RETURNS tables

metrics.name: Net Loss from Returns
metrics.definition: Total financial loss from returned items. Captured in the SR_NET_LOSS, CR_NET_LOSS, WR_NET_LOSS columns.
metrics.calculation: SUM(SR_NET_LOSS) for store returns, SUM(CR_NET_LOSS) for catalog, SUM(WR_NET_LOSS) for web

metrics.name: Promotion ROI
metrics.definition: Revenue generated by promoted transactions relative to the promotion's marketing cost.

sales_channels.description: Physical retail store purchases. Customer is at the point of sale.
Phone and mail orders. Has both a billing customer (CS_BILL_CUSTOMER_SK) and a ship-to customer (CS_SHIP_CUSTOMER_SK) — use BILL for revenue attribution, SHIP for delivery geography.
E-commerce orders. Like catalog, has billing and ship-to customers. References WEB_SITE and WEB_PAGE dimensions.

common_gotchas.solution: ALWAYS add a date filter using D_YEAR or D_MONTH_SEQ in DATE_DIM, joined via SS_SOLD_DATE_SK etc. Without a date filter, a STORE_SALES query will scan 300B rows and be very expensive. Example: JOIN DATE_DIM d ON SS_SOLD_DATE_SK = d.D_DATE_SK WHERE d.D_YEAR = 2001

All _DATE_SK columns (SS_SOLD_DATE_SK, CS_SOLD_DATE_SK, WS_SOLD_DATE_SK, and all return date SKs) can be NULL. Use INNER JOIN to DATE_DIM to automatically exclude NULLs, or add IS NOT NULL explicitly.
SS_CUSTOMER_SK, CS_BILL_CUSTOMER_SK, WS_BILL_CUSTOMER_SK can be NULL for anonymous transactions. Always add IS NOT NULL when joining to CUSTOMER or counting unique customers.

ITEM, STORE, CALL_CENTER, WEB_SITE, and WEB_PAGE are slowly changing dimensions. Always add WHERE I_REC_END_DATE IS NULL (or S_REC_END_DATE IS NULL, WEB_REC_END_DATE IS NULL, etc.) to get only the current version of each record. Failing to do this causes duplicate counts.

common_gotchas.issue: INVENTORY is a snapshot table, not a transaction table
common_gotchas.solution: Do NOT SUM(INV_QUANTITY_ON_HAND) across multiple dates — that would double-count. To get current inventory: use MAX(INV_DATE_SK) per item-warehouse pair, then join back to get the quantity at that latest date.

Each row in STORE_SALES is ONE LINE ITEM, not one order. Use COUNT(*) for line items. Use COUNT(DISTINCT SS_TICKET_NUMBER) for order-level counts. Similarly, COUNT(DISTINCT CS_ORDER_NUMBER) or COUNT(DISTINCT WS_ORDER_NUMBER) for catalog/web orders.

CATALOG_SALES and WEB_SALES both have a billing customer (CS_BILL_CUSTOMER_SK / WS_BILL_CUSTOMER_SK) AND a ship-to customer (CS_SHIP_CUSTOMER_SK / WS_SHIP_CUSTOMER_SK) — they differ for gift orders. Use the BILL customer for revenue and loyalty attribution. Use the SHIP customer for geography analysis.
The STORE dimension column is named S_TAX_PRECENTAGE (note the typo: 'PRECENTAGE' not 'PERCENTAGE'). Use this exact spelling when referencing it.

All Y/N flags in TPC-DS (D_HOLIDAY, D_WEEKEND, C_PREFERRED_CUST_FLAG, P_DISCOUNT_ACTIVE, WP_AUTOGEN_FLAG, etc.) are VARCHAR 'Y'/'N' strings, not SQL booleans. Always compare with = 'Y' or = 'N', never with IS TRUE.

common_gotchas.issue: Customer birth date is split across three columns
common_gotchas.solution: CUSTOMER does not have a single birth date column. Birth date is split across C_BIRTH_YEAR, C_BIRTH_MONTH, and C_BIRTH_DAY. To calculate age: DATEDIFF(year, TRY_TO_DATE(C_BIRTH_YEAR||'-'||LPAD(C_BIRTH_MONTH,2,'0')||'-'||LPAD(C_BIRTH_DAY,2,'0')), CURRENT_DATE()).

SS_NET_PROFIT, CS_NET_PROFIT, WS_NET_PROFIT can be negative (sold below wholesale cost). When calculating average margin, use NULLIF to handle zero denominators. When reporting profitability, call out loss-making items separately.

All TPC-DS sales data in TPCDS_SF100TCL covers approximately calendar years 1998–2002. Always filter on D_YEAR within this range. The 'current' year in the dataset is 2002. Use D_YEAR = 2001 for the most complete full-year comparison.

To calculate total revenue across all channels, query STORE_SALES + CATALOG_SALES + WEB_SALES separately with UNION ALL and sum. Do NOT try to join them — they have different schemas and different order keys.
SS_PROMO_SK IS NULL means no promotion was applied to that line item. To compare promoted vs non-promoted sales: use CASE WHEN SS_PROMO_SK IS NOT NULL THEN 'Promoted' ELSE 'Non-Promoted' END.

product_hierarchy.description: Products in ITEM are organized in a 4-level hierarchy
levels: I_CATEGORY — Top level (10 categories: Women, Men, Children, Shoes, Music, Jewelry, Sports, Books, Home, Electronics)

dimension_sizes.description: Approximate row counts for dimension tables at SF100TCL. Small dimensions are safe in any join.

recommended_query_patterns: Always JOIN DATE_DIM and filter on D_YEAR before any aggregation on fact tables
Use LIMIT on exploratory queries before running aggregations to understand data shape
Use COUNT(DISTINCT ...) for unique entity counts rather than COUNT(*)
For cross-channel totals, use three separate CTEs and UNION ALL — never try to join fact tables
Filter SCD dimensions with REC_END_DATE IS NULL to avoid inflated row counts
For inventory, always derive the latest snapshot per item-warehouse pair before aggregating
